requirement:
The coverage check MUST fail when no usable coverage has been collected, or when
a selected latest attempt has missing, unreadable, or stale coverage. It MUST
distinguish these measurement failures from measured lines with zero execution
and from individual functions absent from otherwise usable coverage. Exception
evidence MUST NOT excuse measurement failures or permit substitution of an
older attempt. Excluded historical runs and incompatible configurations MUST
NOT by themselves cause failure.

Coverage whose format does not support the function attribution required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` MUST be rejected with guidance
to recollect coverage. When missing or corrupt metadata prevents establishing
the latest-per-test selection or active configuration, the check MUST fail
rather than silently use remaining records. Historical data MAY be disregarded
without failure only when its exclusion can be established.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. I read `load_saved` only to see how the active configuration and latest-per-test selection are derived. The expected outcomes below come from the requirement text.

**No usable coverage.**
- `check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stale_missing_legacy_and_uncertain_history_cannot_use_older_success]` asserts that the check fails when no coverage has been recorded.
- `fn[accepted_exceptions_cannot_waive_invalid_measurement_and_checks_still_collect_errors]` covers the "absent" case. It also covers "empty lines" and expects the "No usable instrumented lines" message.

**Selected latest attempt has missing, unreadable or stale coverage.**
- The stale/missing test deletes `profile.profraw` and expects "missing or unreadable".
- The same test changes the source file and expects "stale coverage".
- The exceptions test repeats the missing-profile, stale and "corrupt counters" cases, and expects a "corrupt function attribution" message for the last.
- In every one of these cases an older good attempt exists, and the report still fails. That shows an older attempt is not substituted.
- `fn[readable_failed_execution_can_contribute_but_outcomes_remain_visible]` shows a failed outcome with readable coverage is not a measurement failure. A diagnostic of "broken coverage map" does fail the check.

**Measurement failures are distinguished from zero execution and from absent functions.**
- `fn[accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution]` asserts "zero execution" for a measured zero-count function.
- The same test asserts "not measured" for a function absent from usable coverage, and for a file absent from it.
- `fn[unmeasured_executable_files_and_parse_failures_do_not_disappear]` also asserts "not measured — FAIL" for an absent function.
- Measurement failures produce different messages: "missing or unreadable", "stale coverage", "lacks function attribution" and "No usable…".

**Exception evidence cannot excuse a measurement failure.** The exceptions test runs seven failure kinds with accepted file and function citations in place. For each it asserts the check fails and that the report contains neither "accepted exception" nor a "0/1 (0.0%)" figure.

**Excluded history does not cause failure.**
- A legacy attempt with no function data, recorded under another configuration, leaves a passing report passing.
- After a valid attempt 5, the broken or superseded attempts 2 to 4 for the same test are ignored and the report passes.

**Legacy format.** A legacy attempt with `functions = None` is rejected. The report text contains "lacks function attribution" and, in the exceptions test, "recollect coverage with this Habeas version".

**Corrupt metadata.**
- The stale/missing test writes a corrupt `run.json` and expects "cannot establish latest-per-test". The exceptions test repeats this as "corrupt history".
- In `book.rs`, `fn[malformed_historical_measurements_make_selection_uncertain]` shows several malformed measurement shapes set `uncertain_history`, so remaining records are not silently trusted.
- `fn[selected_attempt_cannot_be_replaced_between_selection_and_loading]` shows that a changed attempt identity is rejected at load time.

**Historical data disregarded only when exclusion is established.** The valid other-configuration legacy data is disregarded, while unreadable or malformed data makes the check fail. Both outcomes are asserted.

I found no obligation of the requirement without a test that exercises it and asserts the outcome.

text: :::{req} check.measurement
The coverage check MUST fail when no usable coverage has been collected, or when
a selected latest attempt has missing, unreadable, or stale coverage. It MUST
distinguish these measurement failures from measured lines with zero execution
and from individual functions absent from otherwise usable coverage. Exception
evidence MUST NOT excuse measurement failures or permit substitution of an
older attempt. Excluded historical runs and incompatible configurations MUST
NOT by themselves cause failure.
Coverage whose format does not support the function attribution required by
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions` MUST be rejected with guidance
to recollect coverage. When missing or corrupt metadata prevents establishing
the latest-per-test selection or active configuration, the check MUST fail
rather than silently use remaining records. Historical data MAY be disregarded
without failure only when its exclusion can be established.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
